title: Safely managed sanitation, Northern Africa and Western Asia, by location
headline: In N. Africa and W. Asia, safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs a rise of 6.5 points a year
subtitle: Proportion of population using an improved sanitation facility that is not shared with other households, from which excreta are safely disposed of in situ or removed and treated off-site
years: So far it has risen 0.9 points a year, from 39.4% in 2000 to 60.7% in 2024.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_SAN_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
flags: headline at 52 px: no candidate fits two lines at 56 px
alt: In N. Africa and W. Asia, safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs a rise of 6.5 points a year. So far it has risen 0.9 points a year, from 39.4% in 2000 to 60.7% in 2024. People using safely managed sanitation, Northern Africa and Western Asia: 39.4% in 2000, 60.7% in 2024. At that pace about 66.0% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 6.5 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has safely managed sanitation moved at anything like 6.5 points a year, and what made it possible?
